history: Joaquín Simó created it at Death & Co in New York around 2010, calling for Smith & Cross navy-strength Jamaican rum. It has since become the standard rum Negroni.
whyItWorks: Jamaican pot-still rum has the same aggressive character Campari does. Neither backs down, and the sweet vermouth keeps them from tearing each other apart.
steps: Stir all three with ice until well chilled.
Strain over a large cube in an old fashioned glass.
Express an orange twist over the surface and drop it in.
techniqueNotes: Smith & Cross is 57% ABV—this is a stronger drink than a gin Negroni by a wide margin.
A softer Jamaican rum (Appleton Signature) makes a pleasant drink but loses the hogo that justifies the swap.

substitutions.notes: Overproof gets the strength but not the funk; gold rum makes a mild Rum Negroni.

name: Kingston Negroni
description: A Negroni built on funky Jamaican rum instead of gin—overripe banana and hogo against the Campari.
creator: Joaquín Simó
